t: A north Indian empire built from the Ganges plain by Chandragupta I and Samudragupta from around 320 CE.
Its age saw Aryabhata's mathematics, Kalidasa's poetry and art that shaped Southeast Asia, earning it the name Golden Age of India.
Huna invasions and feudatories who broke away dissolved it into regional kingdoms by the mid-sixth century.
dyk: Aryabhata, whose Aryabhatiya dates to 499 CE, approximated pi to four decimal places and proposed that the earth rotates on its axis.
ev: Chandragupta I ascends and takes the title Maharajadhiraja, great king of kings
Samudragupta begins the campaigns recorded on the Allahabad Pillar
Chandragupta II succeeds and later defeats the Shaka satraps of western India
Skandagupta takes the throne and repels a major Huna incursion
Hunas under Toramana and Mihirakula occupy much of northwestern and central India
Aulikara king Yashodharman, not a Gupta, defeats Mihirakula
Vishnugupta, the last recognised Gupta emperor, rules only a remnant kingdom
